Propagation Forecast Bulletin 42 ARLP042
From ARRL Headquarters
Newington, CT  October 16, 2026
To all radio amateurs

SB PROP ARL ARLP042
ARLP042 The ARRL Solar Report

Look for improved propagation on the upper HF bands, as both the
sunspot numbers and 10.7-centimeter radio flux remain near or above
100. According to NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC),
the increase in activity is being fueled primarily by sunspot
Region 4551, which is described as the largest and most complex of
six sunspot regions currently visible on the surface of the Sun.
Mostly quiet geomagnetic conditions are expected as well, with some
disturbances possible late next week.

The Australian Space Weather Forecasting Centre predicts mostly
normal HF propagation conditions worldwide.

The W3LPL Propagation Forecast from the Daily DX is predicting
significantly improved DX conditions on 10 and 12 meters for as many
as the next 10 days, with excellent conditions on 17, 15, and 20
meters as well. DX openings on 30 meters should begin in late
afternoon each day, followed by 40 meters around an hour before
sunset, and 80 meters just after sunset.

Weekly Commentary on the Sun, the Magnetosphere, and the Earth's
Ionosphere, October 15, 2026, by F. K. Janda, OK1HH:

The so-called 27-day recurrence derived from the duration of one
rotation of the Sun around its own axis is often a useful tool for
forecasting fluctuations in solar activity. Although rare, there
are instances when the trend is exactly the opposite, which can
be directly misleading for predicting future developments. The
most recent peak solar flux of 136 s.f.u. on October 13 was
measured exactly 27 days after September 17, when the flux was
97 s.f.u. the first day of a relatively long interval with low
values below 100 s.f.u. Consequently, the state of the Earth's
ionosphere and thus shortwave propagation conditions was not as
favorable as might be expected at this time of year.

Furthermore, solar activity will decline for the remainder of
October. Although a disturbance in the Earth's geomagnetic field
can be expected after October 20, it should be brief, and the rest
of the month is expected to bring relatively calm and favorable
conditions.

The Predicted Planetary A Index for October 16 to October 22 is
5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 15, and 20 with a mean of 8.6. The Predicted
Planetary K Index is 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 3, and 4 with a mean of
2.4. 10.7 centimeter flux is 100, 95, 95, 100, 100, 105, and
100 with a mean of 99.3.

For more information concerning shortwave radio propagation, see www.arrl.org/propagation and the ARRL Technical Information Service web page at www.arrl.org/propagation-of-rf-signals. For an explanation of numbers used in this bulletin, see www.arrl.org/the-sun-the-earth-the-ionosphere. Informatiod tutori s on opagation can be found at http://k9la.us.

Also, check this: "Understanding Solar Indices" from September 2002 QST. https://bit.ly/3Rc8Njt

/EX

Propagation Forecast Bulletin 39 ARLP039
From ARRL Headquarters
Newington, CT  September 25, 2026
To all radio amateurs

SB PROP ARL ARLP039
ARLP039 The ARRL Solar Report

Solar activity is likely to continue at low levels with isolated to
occasional C-class flare activity, along with a slight chance for
R1-R2 (Minor-Moderate) M-class flare events, through September 25,
according to NOAASpace Weather Prediction Center. The SWPC reports
that nine sunspot regions are on the visible disk, including a new
Region 4541. There were three solar flares observed in the past week,
none of which was directed toward Earth.

A disturbed solar wind environment was expected to arrive late
yesterday, followed by positive polarity coronal hole high-speed
stream (+CH HSS) influences continuing through September 25.

Unsettled to active geomagnetic field conditions levels are expected
as of today under early +CH HSS effects, including isolated periods
of G1 (Minor) geomagnetic storming today and tomorrow.

The Australian Space Weather Forecasting Centreglobal HF
propagation forecast for middle latitudes is for mild degradation
today due to forecast geomagnetic activity, followed by normal
propagation in the days that follow. We are currently in a period of
equinoctial propagation, during which conditions are relatively
uniform around the world.

Weekly Commentary on the Sun, the Magnetosphere, and the Earth's
Ionosphere, September 24, 2026, by F. K. Janda, OK1HH:

After a prolonged period of calm activity on the Sun as well as in
Earthmagnetosphereanning the entire second third of
Septemberlar activity began to rise first, followed by an increase
in geomagnetic activity starting on September 24. On September 18
only, there were no sunspots on the Sun. The rise in solar activity
on the 24th was accompanied by an intensification of the solar wind,
while the geomagnetic disturbance began its so-called positive phase
(the critical frequencies f0F2 increased significantly between 9:00
and 13:00 UT). Improved shortwave propagation conditions were
observed on September 23.

Solar activity will remain at a higher level for several more days,
while the geomagnetic disturbance will continue only briefly in the
so-called negative phase of development. A calm period is expected to
follow during the last few days of the month. Recovery from the
disturbance will likely be rapid, while a return to improved
shortwave propagation conditions can be expected for most of the
remaining days of the month.

The Predicted Planetary A Index for September 25 to October 1 is 18,
12, 8, 5, 5, 5, and 5 with a mean of 8.3. The Predicted Planetary K
Index is 5, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2, and 2 with a mean of 2.7. 10.7 centimeter
flux is 105, 105, 100, 105, 110, 115, and 115 with a mean of 107.9.

For more information concerning shortwave radio propagation, see www.arrl.org/propagation and the ARRL Technical Information Service web page at www.arrl.org/propagation-of-rf-signals. For an explanation of numbers used in this bulletin, see www.arrl.org/the-sun-the-earth-the-ionosphere. Information and tutorials on propagation can be found at http://k9la.us.

Also, check this: "Understanding Solar Indices" from September 2002 QST. https://bit.ly/3Rc8Njt
